source_text: Credamus itaque Magistro Gentium et reddamus ei testimonium veritatis suae. Vere enim, sicut dixit, humanum est, quod praecepit, ut voluntatis correctio emendaret vitia voluntatis.
pass_a_gloss: Let us therefore believe the Teacher of the Gentiles and render him a testimony of his truth. For truly, as he said, it is human, what he commanded, that a correction of will would amend vices of will.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: Let us therefore believe the Teacher of the Gentiles and bear witness to his truthfulness. Truly, as he said, what he commanded is human: that correcting the will should amend the will’s vices.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Proof-text, especially Rom 5:12 in this book; keep 'testimony' not 'verse'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
